subject: iceCreamCart
pitch: A cheerful seaside ice cream cart. A mint and cream body with a scalloped striped canopy in pink and white, two big spoked wheels, a push handle, a chrome lid over the freezer, a hand-painted sign shaped like a cone, and a row of giant fake ice cream cones in pastel flavours along the top.
reasoning:
I'm planning a single TypeScript module using the SDK to build a cart, since it doesn't need creature-like joints and can rely on plain objects alongside part, paints, lathe, and extrude functions. I'm sketching dimensions: roughly 1.6m long facing +Z, 1.3m tall to the canopy, 0.9m wide.

I'm deciding on a joint hierarchy: a root joint at the origin, with the body attached and wheel joints positioned for axle rotation, keeping the rig minimal since most pieces can just be plain parts on the default bone. Now I'm sketching the body geometry as a mint-colored box sized around 0.86 by 0.5 by 1.1 meters.

Adding wheel geometry...

Still working out spoke orientation...

Now I'm setting up the wheel joints, creating a "wheelL" joint attached to root with a defined position and axis direction, then attaching wheel parts to that bone so they inherit its transform.

Next I'm building the handlebar assembly—constructing the horizontal bar as a rod between two side points, adding support posts connecting it to the body, and placing grip capsules at each end with a distinct color for the handles.

For the chrome lid over the freezer section, I'm figuring out how to build a rounded top cover using a half-cylinder shape rotated to lie flat on the body's top surface, since a simple box would look too blocky for that rounded chrome detail.

Now I need a scalloped striped canopy in pink and white over the cart body, positioned above as a sloped awning with scallop-edged outline and painted stripes along the front.

Writing the scallop geometry...

Setting pink and white stripe parameters for the paint, then considering a canopy roof as a thin striped box geometry above the structure.

Adding chrome support poles at the four body corners connecting to the roof, then positioning a scalloped valance to hang from the roof's front edge.

For the giant ice cream cones, I'm thinking of placing a row of them on top of the roof as whimsical decoration, each with a cone shape and pastel scoop on top, though I'm weighing whether that's too tall versus putting them along the front of the body instead.

Still refining the cone geometry...

I'll place each scoop as a sphere resting on top of its cone, picking fun flavor colors like mint, strawberry, lemon, blueberry, and peach for variety.

I'm arranging five cones in a row along the top of the roof, spaced evenly, and considering adding a cone-shaped sign on the side panel as a hand-painted decorative touch.

I'm placing the cone-shaped sign on the front face of the body, extruding its outline near the top, and deciding how to paint it with a hand-painted look—maybe wavy colored bands or a custom gradient instead of a texture, since the extrude geometry lacks UVs.

Switching approach: I'll use a flat PlaneGeometry mounted on the front with an SVG texture, since boxes/planes support UV mapping properly. I'm sketching the SVG design—a scoop circle, a cone triangle with cross-hatching, maybe "ICE" text, and a border stroke.

Now I'm figuring out placement: the sign's aspect ratio (100:140) maps to a 0.5x0.7 plane, and I'm deciding whether to mount it on the cart body or on a standalone post beside it. I settle on positioning it on a pole off to the side, rotated so the plane's normal faces outward in the +X direction instead of the default +Z.

Simplifying the stand: two posts at z=0.1 and z=0.5 running from the ground up to y=0.3, with the sign plane hung between them above that height.

Good enough for the sign and posts. Now I'm adding body details: a dark serving window on the front face and a cream counter ledge beneath it to suggest a food truck hatch.

For the body coloring, I'm going with a mint body and cream trim along the base and top border to keep it simple and clean.

I'm fixing the wheel geometry so the torus doesn't sink too far below the ground plane—adjusting the radius and tube size so the bottom sits right at y=0 within tolerance.

Now I'm placing the wheel joints symmetrically on either side of the cart body, defining them as children of the root joint with explicit positions and rotation directions so the torus and spoke parts attach rigidly without extra weighting complexity.

For the wheel details, I'm building six spokes using a rotated box geometry spread at 60-degree increments to form a classic spoked-wheel look, then adding a small cylindrical hub rotated to align its axis with the wheel face. I'm settling on a pink-and-cream color palette for the wheels with a chrome hub for contrast, and planning to use the lathe helper for the ice-cream cone shapes mounted on top.

I'm now checking the cone's geometry points for validity and positioning the waffle-colored cone tip near the roof so a scoop sphere can sit naturally overlapping the cone's top, adjusting the vertical offsets so the scoop visually rests on the cone rather than floating above or sinking through it.

For the lid, I'm shaping a hemisphere dome with scaling to flatten it into an oval canopy, positioning it so its edges clear the body and roof without collision. Then I'm setting up striped paint patterns for the roof and valance using an axis-based banding function, reusing the same pink-and-white stripe paint instance across both surfaces so the pattern stays consistent, though I'm wary it might look overly busy on the canopy.

Now I'm computing a scalloped outline for the valance by generating a series of wave-shaped points across its width—dividing it into six scallops, sampling sine-curve dips between each segment's edges, and pushing the resulting coordinates into an array that defines the decorative wavy bottom edge.

I need to pass x: [1,0,0] explicitly so the outline's local x-axis aligns with world X, keeping the normal direction correct. For the sign itself, I'm sketching an SVG with a rounded cream background, a triangular ice cream cone shape, and a pink scoop with a highlight circle on top.

Actually, I want the sign's entire shape to be cone-shaped rather than putting a cone image on a rectangle — so I'm redrawing it as a scoop circle plus a cone triangle forming the board outline itself, filled with transparent background, waffle texture lines, and bold "ICE" text on the scoop, sized to match the 0.5x0.7 aspect ratio of the sign plane.

For placement, I'm positioning the sign plane facing +X with two support posts tucked slightly behind it at x=0.8 so they don't poke through the front, running from the ground up to the sign's bottom edge, and I'm adding a second mirrored plane facing -X so the sign reads correctly from both sides.

For the final export, I'm defining the default builder function that assembles the ice-cream cart and returns the baked root. I'm skipping sweeps, drips, and sprinkles to keep things simple, but adding a serving window as a dark recessed box on the front face with a small cream-colored counter ledge beneath it, and refining the base trim box so it sits snugly under the body without clipping into it.

Now I'm positioning the wheels so their hubs and torus tubes align properly with the body's bottom edge and width, then adding the chrome lid and working out the rear push-handle posts and canopy support poles using chrome-colored rods, making sure the handle posts and canopy poles don't collide despite sharing similar x-positions.

I'm sizing the roof box and front valance so they overlap correctly with the roof's bottom edge, then placing the row of waffle cones along the roof top with five distinct ice cream flavors (mint, strawberry, lemon, blueberry, peach), adding a cherry sphere on top of one scoop, and confirming the overall cart height comes out to roughly 1.4 meters.

For the scoops I'm using a spherical geometry slightly squashed for shape, and setting up part defaults so bones default to the nearest joint unless I explicitly assign wheel parts to their wheel joints, while sharing materials by color string. Now I'm working out the lathe outline input format for the body profile.

I'm defining the paint patterns next — a solid mint for the body and candy stripes for the roof using a stripes helper with configurable size, axis, and width — then setting up the extruded valance trim with its own position and orientation, plus the sign posts as simple rods. Writing the final assembly code...

Still laying out cart geometry...

I'm working out the spoke placement, rotating each box by 30° increments around the axis so six lines through the center effectively create twelve radial spokes spanning the wheel's diameter.

Now I'm placing the hub cylinder centered at the wheel's axis, and double-checking that the spoke rotation stays correctly oriented within the YZ plane. I'm moving on to building the push handle rods, positioning chrome rods symmetrically on both sides and connecting them at the back.

Adding handle grips, canopy poles...

Good, the cone outline forms a solid closed shape. Now I'm adding a small cherry sphere on top of the middle flavor, then setting up a sign with a texture plane rotated to face outward, mounted on posts near the stand.

I'm now checking whether mirroring the plane by rotating it -90° about Y for the back-facing sign properly flips the UV orientation so the image reads correctly from that viewing angle rather than appearing reversed.

Beyond that I'm verifying the post placements stay aligned behind the sign geometry, confirming the svg texture import comes from the SDK's exported helpers, and double-checking the stripes/paint reuse across the awning, valance, and roof components.

Checking the extrude outline typing and ground clearance, then adding the cone sign with a hand-painted svg feel before finalizing clean, tidy code using default detail settings.
